agree_diff.denominator: decided replies (observed and predicted over the same replies)
agree_diff.desc: Observed minus predicted share of the larger camp's option, over the same decided replies.
agree_diff.label: Observed minus predicted

agree_obs.desc: The larger camp's option, its observed share of decided replies.
agree_obs.label: Shared option, observed

agree_pred.desc: The larger camp's option, as the seats fit predicts its share of decided replies.
agree_pred.label: Shared option, predicted

boundary_diff.denominator: decided replies, paired within the scenario
boundary_diff.desc: How much more often the first-listed line wins inside one message than across two, paired within the scenario.
boundary_diff.label: One message minus separate messages

ctx_later_bare.desc: The later line wins in pairs without the operator, bare.
ctx_later_bare.label: Later wins, bare

ctx_later_context.desc: The later line wins in pairs without the operator, in context.
ctx_later_context.label: Later wins, in context

ctx_later_diff.denominator: decided replies, paired within the item
ctx_later_diff.desc: Later wins, in context minus bare, paired within the item.
ctx_later_diff.label: Later wins, context minus bare

ctx_op_bare.desc: The operator line, sent first, wins with the bare instructions.
ctx_op_bare.label: Operator first, bare

ctx_op_context.desc: The operator line, sent first, wins with each instruction inside realistic text.
ctx_op_context.label: Operator first, in context

ctx_op_diff.denominator: decided replies, paired within the item
ctx_op_diff.desc: Operator first, in context minus bare, paired within the item.
ctx_op_diff.label: Operator first, context minus bare

first_merged.desc: The first-listed of the user line and the memory note wins when both are inside the task's message.
first_merged.label: First, one message

first_separate.desc: The first-listed of the user line and the memory note wins when each is in its own message.
first_separate.label: First, separate messages

flagged.desc: Share of decided Ladder pair replies (except the two system lines) that flag or hedge the conflict, by our keyword patterns.
flagged.label: Flagged or hedged

late_op.denominator: decided replies, paired within the scenario
late_op.desc: The real operator line sent last minus sent first.
late_op.label: Late op. gain

later_before_task.desc: The later line wins when both lines come before the task.
later_before_task.label: Later wins: both before the task

later_follows_task.desc: The later line wins when it follows the task (the task comes first or between the two lines).
later_follows_task.label: Later wins: follows the task

later_wins.desc: The later of two lines wins in free Ladder pairs (user, tool result, memory note; both orders).
later_wins.label: Later wins

load_chosen.denominator: conflict groups in tool and file-write trials
load_chosen.desc: Share of tool and file-write conflict groups in which the reply chose one of the group's options.
load_chosen.label: Groups chosen

op_first.desc: The operator line (S1 or S2), first in the Ladder, wins against a later user, tool or memory line.
op_first.label: Operator first

op_first_usable.desc: The same, over every usable reply: a reply where no single seat won counts as a loss.
op_first_usable.label: Operator first, all usable replies

op_label_first.desc: The operator line wins when sent first as the same labelled text in a user message.
op_label_first.label: Label, first

op_label_last.desc: The operator line wins when sent last as labelled text in a user message.
op_label_last.label: Label, last

op_real_first.desc: The operator line wins when sent first in the real system message.
op_real_first.label: Real, first

op_real_last.desc: The operator line wins when sent last in the real system message.
op_real_last.label: Real, last

out_chose.desc: Share of usable Ladder conflict replies that chose exactly one option shown in the trial.
out_chose.label: Chose

out_multiple.desc: Share of usable Ladder conflict replies that carried two or more options' answers.
out_multiple.label: Multiple

out_no_action.desc: Share of usable Ladder conflict replies that took no action of the kind the task reads.
out_no_action.label: No action

out_off_menu.desc: Share of usable Ladder conflict replies that gave a clean answer no option in the trial asked for.
out_off_menu.label: Off-menu

out_unresolved.desc: Share of usable Ladder conflict replies that no classifier could label.
out_unresolved.label: Unresolved

real_label_first.denominator: decided replies, paired within the scenario
real_label_first.desc: The operator line sent first in the real system message minus the same labelled text in a user message, over all task types.
real_label_first.label: Real minus label, first (all task types)

real_label_fmt.denominator: decided replies, paired within the scenario
real_label_fmt.desc: Real minus label with the operator first, in format tasks.
real_label_fmt.label: Real minus label, format

real_label_last.denominator: decided replies, paired within the scenario
real_label_last.desc: Real minus label with the operator line sent last.
real_label_last.label: Real minus label, last

real_label_or.denominator: decided replies, paired within the scenario
real_label_or.desc: Real minus label with the operator first, in ordering and refusal tasks.
real_label_or.label: Real minus label, ordering and refusal

real_label_tp.denominator: decided replies, paired within the scenario
real_label_tp.desc: In tool-call and file-write tasks, the operator line sent first in the real system message minus the same text sent first as a labelled user message.
real_label_tp.label: Real minus label, tool and file-write

s3_over_s4.desc: The user line beats the tool result in free Ladder pairs, both orders weighted equally.
s3_over_s4.label: User over tool result

s3_over_s5.desc: The user line beats the memory note in free Ladder pairs, both orders weighted equally.
s3_over_s5.label: User over memory note

s5_over_s4.desc: The memory note beats the tool result in free Ladder pairs, both orders weighted equally (one minus the tool's share).
s5_over_s4.label: Memory note over tool result

seat_gain.denominator: usable replies in the triples and five-way sets, forecast from the pairs
seat_gain.desc: Nats per reply that one strength per seat adds to the position fit when forecasting triples and five-way sets from pairs.
seat_gain.label: Seat gain

share_position.denominator: usable replies in the triples and five-way sets, forecast from the pairs
share_position.desc: Share of the gap from a uniform guess to the empirical reference that the position fit recovers when forecasting three- and five-way conflicts from pairs.
share_position.label: Position fit, share of gap

share_seats.denominator: usable replies in the triples and five-way sets, forecast from the pairs
share_seats.desc: The same for the seats fit, which adds one strength per seat to position.
share_seats.label: Seats fit, share of gap

share_task.denominator: usable replies in the triples and five-way sets, forecast from the pairs
share_task.desc: The same for the task-aware fit, which also knows whether a line comes before or after the task line.
share_task.label: Task-aware fit, share of gap

sys_second.desc: The second of the two system-message lines (S1 and S2, each order half the time) wins.
sys_second.label: 2nd system line wins

task_gain.denominator: usable replies in the triples and five-way sets, forecast from the pairs
task_gain.desc: Nats per reply that knowing where the task line is adds to the position fit.
task_gain.label: Task gain

tier_gap1.desc: The tier rule is followed when the two declared tiers are 1 apart.
tier_gap1.label: Tier rule, gap 1

tier_gap2.desc: The tier rule is followed when the two declared tiers are 2 apart.
tier_gap2.label: Tier rule, gap 2

tier_gap3.desc: The tier rule is followed when the two declared tiers are 3 apart.
tier_gap3.label: Tier rule, gap 3

tier_gap4.desc: The tier rule is followed when the two declared tiers are 4 apart.
tier_gap4.label: Tier rule, gap 4

tier_gap5.desc: The tier rule is followed when the two declared tiers are 5 apart.
tier_gap5.label: Tier rule, gap 5

tier_rule.desc: The option of the lower declared tier wins (decided replies).
tier_rule.label: Tier rule

tier_rule_usable.desc: The same over every usable reply.
tier_rule_usable.label: Tier rule, all usable

user_tool.desc: The user line (S3) beats the tool result (S4), both orders.
user_tool.label: User beats tool
